messages:
maya: Customer reports their long-running batch upload hit 429s right before monthly refill. UI showed credits refilled at 00:00 but API kept returning 429 for ~10 minutes. They're on standard plan, single org, no recent plan change.

maya: repro steps they gave: start large multipart upload that triggers retries on some chunks; after many retries the tenant quota drains then shows zero in UI, then at midnight UI shows refill but API still 429 until ~00:09.

maya: pasted a small excerpt from their client logs:
```
2026-03-01T23:58:42Z POST /v1/generate 200 x-token=1243 req_id=abc123
2026-03-01T23:59:10Z POST /v1/generate 429 x-token=0 req_id=def456
2026-03-02T00:00:01Z GET /v1/credits 200 remaining=1000
2026-03-02T00:00:05Z POST /v1/generate 429 x-token=0 req_id=ghi789
2026-03-02T00:09:21Z POST /v1/generate 200 x-token=998 req_id=jkl012
```

maya: customer says they were doing aggressive client-side retries (exponential backoff but small cap) and used no idempotency keys. They want to know why UI says refilled but API kept denying.

support-bot: FYI docs on quota refill & edge cache: https://redwood.example.com/docs/quotas#refill-window :edge_cache: (same-day midnight UTC refill unless tenant TZ override).

devon: looking. Can you paste the API request-id headers from one of the failing 429 responses? We need x-rw-req and edge headers. Also which region were they hitting?

maya: gave sample header from failing call: "x-rw-req: def456"; "x-edge-cache: MISS"; region: us-west-2.

devon: thanks. Two quick hypotheses: (1) retries + long-running connection exhausted token bucket before refill; (2) edge cache / quota cache inconsistent: UI reads central billing store which was updated at refill, but edge nodes still had stale local counters until their TTL reset. Both would explain UI=refilled + API=429.

devon: can you confirm whether the failing requests are hitting our edge rate limiter vs central quota service? If x-edge-cache: MISS they hit origin but we still have multiple layers. Also check whether requests used the same API key across parallel workers (would share token bucket).

maya: customer says one API key, many parallel workers (20+), each retrying. They confirmed no idempotency keys.

devon: that matches classic burst depletion. Our token accounting counts tokens on each accepted response; retries that result in 429 still may have attempted reserved capacity on edge. We also recently tightened the burst cap for standard plan to avoid tail-latency overloads — that could make refill appear slower for large concurrent reconnect storms.

sasha: billing chiming in — did they upgrade recently or switch to reserved/dedicated? That changes burst allowances.

maya: no upgrade. Standard plan.

devon: quick mitigation we can recommend to customer: 1) add jittered/backoff with larger max interval; 2) reduce parallelism or switch to a single worker with request queueing; 3) use idempotency keys for chunked retries so server can short-circuit duplicate work; 4) if they need sustained high throughput, consider Dedicated capacity.

devon: operational action for us: check edge quota cache TTL and refill propagation window for us-west-2; also inspect token-bucket logs for org to see exact depletion timeline. I'll pull logs.

oncall: I pulled the quota service logs for org_id=org-ACME, window=monthly. Shows heavy token burn at 23:58-23:59 with many partial failures. Edge cache invalidation events at 00:00:03 but some edge nodes didn't contact origin until 00:08:xx due to backoff in our health probe (explains 00:09 recovery).

oncall: snippet from internal audit log: "quota_update org-ACME set remaining=1000 at 2026-03-02T00:00:00Z origin; edge-cache-invalidate queued -> some nodes delayed up to 9m due to rate-limited MRU sync"

maya: so root cause = combination of burst exhaustion + delayed edge cache invalidation. Customer-facing explanation ready?

sasha: yes, propose this message: "Your monthly bucket refilled at midnight, but because many parallel retrying clients had exhausted the edge-level allowance and some edge nodes still had stale counters, the API returned 429 for a short period after the refill. We recommend reducing parallel retries and adding idempotency keys; if you need guaranteed immediate post-refill throughput, upgrade to Dedicated or contact sales for burst increases."

maya: sent that to customer. They asked for a timeline of our fix options.

devon: engineering mitigation options: short-term: tweak edge TTL and increase invalidation fanout for critical refill events (can be hotfixed, low risk). Medium-term: implement origin-side authoritative token check that treats refill events as immediate for any origin-authenticated request, overriding edge counters for a small window after refill. Long-term: surface "refill-complete" websocket/webhook to subscribed tenants so clients can resume aggressive retries only when refill confirmed.

devon: I'll open an internal ticket with proposed hotfix to increase invalidation fanout for monthly refill events. ETA for hotfix: 4-8 hours of work + deploy.

oncall: created ticket INF-8743 and set priority P2. Will run canary in us-west-2 then global.

billing: also note we can offer a temporary burst credit top-up for impacted customers while we hotfix. Maya, do you want me to reach out to ACME on a goodwill top-up?

maya: yes please, offer one-time 10k token top-up and mention we're working on a fix.

devon: follow-up: we should also add guidance to support KB: what to tell customers who see UI refill earlier than API accepts traffic — include troubleshooting checklist: check x-edge-cache header, consolidate API key usage, use idempotency, reduce parallelism, and ask support to escalate for hotfix.

maya: noted — will add KB entry and link to ticket.

support-bot: Incident timeline/bundle: https://redwood.example.com/incidents/INF-8743 (internal).

maya: customer replied: appreciated, accepted top-up, will throttle retries for now. Asked whether we can proactively notify before next refill if we're planning changes.

sasha: we should notify large tenants about any planned quota refactor windows. I'll add an outreach item to the ticket.

devon: closing loop: hotfix scheduled, customer mitigations recommended, billing top-up offered. Reopen if recurrence after deploy. :white_check_mark:
